title: Pop Sound
blurb: Pure pop, gone almost before it registers, and by some distance one of the most-used sounds on the internet. Interface designers reach for it because it makes a tap feel physical; video editors use it to make text appear, bullet points land, or objects arrive on screen. TikTok's entire visual grammar of things springing into frame runs on some version of this noise. It is deliberately characterless — no bass, no tail, nothing to date it — which is precisely why it has outlived every trend that ever used it.
origin: A short pop or bubble sound effect, widely used in UI and video editing.
